questions.q: What does 'multi-tenant' mean in the context of Oracle Fusion Cloud?
options: Many customers share Oracle-managed infrastructure, with their data kept securely isolated from each other
Each customer gets a dedicated, separate copy of the hardware and software
Only tenants who pay an extra fee can use the cloud version
Customers must share their business data with each other
questions.explain: Multi-tenant SaaS means many customers run on shared, Oracle-managed infrastructure while their individual data stays isolated — this is what makes SaaS economics work.

questions.q: Which of these responsibilities belongs to Oracle, not the customer, in the Fusion Cloud SaaS model?
options: Deciding Chart of Accounts structure
Patching the operating system and database
Assigning security roles to employees
Training AP clerks on the new process
questions.explain: Oracle manages the data center, operating system, database, the application itself, and its updates — the customer handles setup, security, data, and training.

questions.q: Why is deep code-level customization largely unavailable in Oracle Fusion Cloud, compared to an on-premises product?
options: Oracle charges extra for any code changes
Fusion Cloud has no underlying code at all
It's a multi-tenant product sharing one codebase; letting one customer modify it would affect every other tenant
Customization was removed because customers asked for simpler products
questions.explain: Because many customers share the same codebase and infrastructure, Oracle cannot let an individual customer modify the shared code — hence the shift to configuration and sanctioned extension tools.

questions.q: Which of these is a sanctioned Oracle Fusion Cloud extension tool mentioned in the lesson?
options: Manual file transfers between customers
A locally installed custom database server
A third-party code editor for modifying the shared codebase
Oracle Transactional Business Intelligence (OTBI)
questions.explain: OTBI for reporting, Visual Builder for extensions, and REST APIs for integration are examples of Oracle's sanctioned tools that sit alongside — not inside — the core application.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where does nearly all of a Financials functional consultant's work fall?
options: The customer's side of the responsibility list: setup, security, and making business processes work
Upgrading the underlying database
Patching Oracle's servers
Managing Oracle's data center uptime
questions.explain: A functional consultant works almost entirely in the customer's responsibility column — configuration, security, and process design — not Oracle's infrastructure management.
